report: Aegis Wealth AI: AI model and asset-allocation logic disclosure

advisor.data_sent: Each turn: the client's tier, capacity and willingness scores, maximum acceptable loss, profile status, current proposal number and status, the last 10 chat messages, and the results of the tools it calls.
advisor.data_never_sent: Names, email addresses, passwords, session or confirmation tokens, and other clients' data.

tools.name: search_products
tools.description: Search the shelf of 20 sample products. Returns code, name, type, risk level (1-5), annual fee %, liquidity days, lock-up months and whether each suits the client's tier. All filters are optional (null).

tools.name: compare_products
tools.description: Compare 2 or 3 products for an amount (CNY 10,000-10,000,000) and a horizon (1-30 whole years): fee cost, end value after fees under an assumed gross return, liquidity, lock-up and suitability. Assumed returns are illustrations, not forecasts.

tools.name: explain_rule
tools.description: Return the text and threshold of one compliance-gate rule, R-01 to R-09, and the regulatory requirement it is designed to meet.

tools.name: get_profile_summary
tools.description: Return the client's own risk profile: tier, capacity and willingness scores, open contradictions and maximum acceptable loss.

tools.name: get_proposal
tools.description: Return one of the client's own proposals: items with the reason each was chosen, risk metrics, the three hypothetical stress results and the compliance-gate result with every rule.

tools.name: project_goal
tools.description: Project the client's own proposal (or, with no proposal, their tier's mix for an amount) over a horizon: 1,000 illustrative paths resampled from history, net of fees. Returns the chance of reaching a target, the bad (P10), typical (P50) and good (P90) end values, the chance of ending below the money paid in, and the monthly contribution needed for a 50%, 75% or 90% chance. Illustrative, not a forecast. Optional inputs are null.

tools.name: suggest_fix
tools.description: How to fix one of the client's own proposals: the smallest change, computed by code, that gets it through the compliance gate, with each change and the rule it fixes. Read-only: the client applies it with the Apply button on the card, and the gate checks the new version again. Null means the latest open proposal.

tools.name: check_drift
tools.description: Check how far the client's own invested portfolio has drifted from the mix they last agreed to (their latest executed proposal), at the simulated market's current prices: each asset class's target and live weight, the drift in percentage points against the band, rules the live holdings now fail, and the trades a rebalancing would place. Read-only: nothing is saved or traded. Prices are simulated from illustrative history.

tools.name: create_proposal
tools.description: Create a new proposal from an amount (CNY), a horizon in whole years and the amount needed within 2 years. The compliance gate always runs; nothing is executed. Requires a complete, current risk profile.

tools.name: revise_proposal
tools.description: Save a new version of one of the client's open proposals with new product weights (they must total 100). The compliance gate always runs on the new version; nothing is executed.

tools.name: propose_rebalance
tools.description: Propose a rebalancing of the client's own portfolio back to their latest executed mix: saves a new proposal version with the trades, and the compliance gate always runs on it. Nothing is executed: the client opens it, takes the quiz and presses Confirm. Returns the open rebalancing if one is already priced at today's prices.

permission_tiers.scope: Read the product shelf and the compliance rules.
Read the client's own profile and proposals; the session's user id limits every query.
Create or revise a proposal; needs a complete, contradiction-free profile under 365 days old, and the gate always runs.
Execute orders. No tool exists: only the client's own Confirm click creates the single-use token.

grounding.allowed_numbers: Every number in a reply must match a value in that turn's tool results or the client's message, rounded the same way; whole numbers up to 10 and years 2000-2030 need no source.
grounding.on_failure: The reply is rewritten once with a note naming the problem; if it fails again, a checked template answers.

steps: Start from the model portfolio for the client's tier (cash, bonds, gold, equities).
Under a 3-year horizon, cap equities plus gold at 20%, equities first, and move the excess to bonds (cash for tier 1).
Raise cash to cover the amount needed within 2 years (the liquidity floor), taking it pro rata from the other classes.
Round each class to a whole percent, half away from zero; a remainder goes to cash, and an excess comes off the largest non-cash class.

In each class, choose the lowest-fee eligible product, then the fastest to access: risk level at or below the tier, lock-up within the horizon, minimum investment within the slot, and only same- or next-day cash when money is needed soon.
Split a class above 40% between its two lowest-fee eligible products, so no product exceeds 40%.
If a class has no eligible product, move its weight to cash.

rules.name: Allocation total
rules.description: The weights add up to 100% within 0.01.

basis.title: Internal control set by the Aegis team
basis.requirement: A proposal invests the whole amount exactly once, so every other check measures the real portfolio.

rules.name: Suitability
rules.description: Every product's risk level is at or below the client's tier.

basis.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
basis.requirement: Asset management that uses AI must follow the general rules on investor suitability.

basis.title: Measures for the Suitability Management of Securities and Futures Investors (CSRC, 2016)
basis.requirement: Match each product's risk level to the investor's risk tolerance, and do not recommend products above it.

basis.title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
basis.requirement: Recommend only investments that suit the client's risk tolerance and ability to bear losses.

rules.name: Concentration
rules.description: Every non-cash product is at most 40% of the portfolio.

basis.title: Internal control set by the Aegis team
basis.requirement: No single non-cash product may exceed 40% of a portfolio, so one product cannot dominate the outcome.

rules.name: Liquidity reserve
rules.description: The liquid share of the portfolio covers the near-term need.

basis.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565
basis.requirement: The suitability assessment covers the client's financial situation, including liquid assets and regular commitments.

rules.name: Horizon
rules.description: Under a 3-year horizon, equity plus gold is at most 20%.

basis.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565
basis.requirement: The suitability assessment covers the client's objectives, including how long they want to hold the investment.

basis.title: Internal control set by the Aegis team
basis.requirement: Under a 3-year horizon, equity and gold together stay at or below 20%.

rules.name: Lock-up
rules.description: Every product's lock-up fits within the client's horizon.

basis.title: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565
basis.requirement: The suitability assessment covers how long the client wants to hold the investment, so no lock-up may outlast it.

rules.name: Fee level
rules.description: The weighted annual fee should not exceed 1.00%.

basis.title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
basis.requirement: Tell clients about all costs and related charges in good time.

basis.title: Internal control set by the Aegis team
basis.requirement: A weighted annual fee above 1.00% is flagged for the client to acknowledge.

rules.name: Drawdown tolerance
rules.description: The historical maximum drawdown should not exceed the client's maximum acceptable loss.

basis.title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
basis.requirement: Take the client's ability to bear losses into account.

basis.title: Measures for the Suitability Management of Securities and Futures Investors (CSRC, 2016)
basis.requirement: Assess the investor's risk tolerance before recommending products.

rules.name: Stress tolerance
rules.description: The worst stress-scenario loss should not exceed the client's maximum acceptable loss.

basis.title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
basis.requirement: Take the client's ability to bear losses into account.

basis.title: Measures for the Suitability Management of Securities and Futures Investors (CSRC, 2016)
basis.requirement: Assess the investor's risk tolerance before recommending products.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: Report the AI model's main parameters and asset-allocation logic to the regulator.
ai_controls.control: Model disclosure report (model, prompt fingerprint, tools, allocation logic and rules), exported from the Control Room.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: Open a separate account for each investor's AI-managed investing.
ai_controls.control: Each client has a separate sandbox account; executed orders touch nothing else.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: Make investors fully aware of the AI algorithm's inherent defects and risks.
ai_controls.control: Disclosure DISC-04 on the Confirm screen, read before every execution.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: Follow the general rules on investor suitability and information disclosure.
ai_controls.control: The compliance gate (R-02, R-08, R-09) checks every proposal, the AI's included.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: Do not use AI to exaggerate products or mislead investors; never promise principal or returns.
ai_controls.control: Every AI reply passes the grounding check: unsupported numbers and promise words never reach the client.

ai_controls.title: Guiding Opinions on Regulating the Asset Management Business of Financial Institutions (PBOC, CBIRC, CSRC and SAFE, 2018)
ai_controls.requirement: When model defects or system faults cause herd behaviour that threatens market stability, step in by hand to adjust or stop the AI business.
ai_controls.control: Suspend AI advisor and Halt execution switches, each with a logged reason.

ai_controls.title: Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
ai_controls.requirement: Record events automatically over the system's lifetime.
ai_controls.control: Append-only operation log of every tool call, broker decision, gate result and order.
ai_controls.note: Applied as good practice: investment advice is not on the Act's high-risk list.

ai_controls.title: Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
ai_controls.requirement: Let people oversee the system and stop it.
ai_controls.control: Only the client's own Confirm click places orders, and compliance can stop the advisor at any time.
ai_controls.note: Applied as good practice: investment advice is not on the Act's high-risk list.

ai_controls.title: Artificial Intelligence Act (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689)
ai_controls.requirement: Tell people they are interacting with an AI system, and mark AI-generated content in a machine-readable way.
ai_controls.control: The chat opens with an AI notice, every reply carries its label, and its provenance travels with it and in X-AI-* response headers.

ai_controls.title: Markets in Financial Instruments Directive (Directive 2014/65/EU)
ai_controls.requirement: Before the transaction, give a retail client a statement on how the advice suits them.
ai_controls.control: A hash-chained advice record holds the proposal, the gate result, the disclosures and the quiz.

ai_controls.title: Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (CAC, MIIT, MPS and NRTA, 2025)
ai_controls.requirement: Add explicit labels that users can see to AI-generated text, in the content or the interface.
ai_controls.control: Each reply is labelled AI-generated, Automated template (checked) or System notice where the client reads it.

ai_controls.title: Measures for Labelling AI-Generated Synthetic Content (CAC, MIIT, MPS and NRTA, 2025)
ai_controls.requirement: Add implicit labels to the metadata of AI-generated content.
ai_controls.control: Each reply's provenance (label, serving model, configuration fingerprint, SHA-256 of the text) is stored with it and sent as response headers.

ai_controls.title: Capital Market FinTech Development Plan 2026-2030 (CSRC, 2026)
ai_controls.requirement: File the advisory algorithm and disclose how it works.
ai_controls.control: The model disclosure states the configuration fingerprint that every reply records, so a filing can be matched to the answers it produced.

ai_controls.title: Capital Market FinTech Development Plan 2026-2030 (CSRC, 2026)
ai_controls.requirement: Combine human oversight with AI advice.
ai_controls.control: The review queue: AI turns flagged by code are cleared or escalated by the compliance officer, and only the client's own click executes.

ai_controls.title: Circular to licensed corporations on the use of generative AI language models (SFC, 2024)
ai_controls.requirement: For AI investment advice, keep management oversight, human review of output and continuous monitoring.
ai_controls.control: The Control Room's live feed and alerts, and human review of every flagged turn.
ai_controls.note: Applied as good practice: Aegis is a sandbox, not a licensed corporation.

ai_controls.title: 2026 Annual Regulatory Oversight Report: generative AI and AI agents (FINRA, 2025)
ai_controls.requirement: Track agent actions and decisions, keep prompt and output logs, and record which model version was used and when.
ai_controls.control: Each turn's trace (model calls, tool calls, the number check), stored with the reply, the serving model and the configuration fingerprint.

ai_controls.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
ai_controls.requirement: Detect and contain attempts to redirect the agent's goals.
ai_controls.control: Threat signals on every message for the review queue; the broker and the gate stop the attempt whatever the model writes.

ai_controls.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
ai_controls.requirement: Constrain what each tool can do and validate its inputs.
ai_controls.control: Eleven strict tools in permission tiers T0 to T2, with server-side limits; no tool can execute an order.

ai_controls.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
ai_controls.requirement: Scope every agent action to the user's own identity and privileges.
ai_controls.control: The session's user id limits every query; a request for another client's data is refused by the broker and logged.

ai_controls.title: OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026)
ai_controls.requirement: Keep a human in control of consequential actions and stop the agent overstating itself.
ai_controls.control: Orders need the client's Confirm click and a one-time token; promise words and unsupported figures never reach the client.

ai_controls.title: Guidelines on Online Distribution and Advisory Platforms (SFC, effective 6 April 2019)
ai_controls.requirement: Treat rebalancing as a recommendation that triggers the suitability requirement, and keep effective rebalancing practices.
ai_controls.control: A rebalancing is a new proposal version: the nine-rule gate checks it against the client's current tier, How to fix applies if it fails, and only the client's quiz and Confirm execute it.
ai_controls.note: Applied as good practice: Aegis is a sandbox, not a licensed platform.

ai_controls.title: Report on Digital Investment Advice (FINRA, March 2016)
ai_controls.requirement: Establish the customer's intent to rebalance, disclose how rebalancing works and any drift threshold, and set how the tool acts in a major market movement.
ai_controls.control: The 5-point drift band is one number in rules.json, shown beside every drift figure. Nothing rebalances without the client's own request and Confirm, and trades priced before the market moved cannot execute.

config_components.grounding_policy: grounding-2026-10: every number traced to a tool result or the client's message; banned phrases blocked

governance.labelling: Every reply carries a visible label (AI-generated, automated template or system notice) and machine-readable provenance: the serving model, the configuration fingerprint and the SHA-256 of the text, also sent as X-AI-* response headers. The chat opens with a notice that the client is talking to an AI system.
review_triggers: A medium or high threat signal on the client's message
A tool call the permission broker blocked
A proposal by the AI that the gate rejected
A reply rewritten, or replaced by a template, after the number check
A reply the client marked as unhelpful
governance.tracing: Each turn is recorded as spans named after the OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (invoke_agent, chat, execute_tool) plus aegis.grounding and aegis.template, with durations, tiers, decisions and token use. Prompts and tool arguments are not captured.
